## Workflow {#sec-workflow}

This section documents how the manuscript is built and should be removed
before submission. The source is the Quarto file `index.qmd`, and
`_quarto.yml` configures a Quarto *manuscript* project that renders HTML,
Word, JATS and a RevTeX PDF from that single source.

### Building

Render all formats, or only the PDF, with
```bash
quarto render
quarto render index.qmd --to pdf
```
Output is written to `_manuscript/`. Because `freeze: true` is set, a
project-wide render reuses stored code output; rendering `index.qmd`
explicitly re-executes the Python chunks. Use `quarto preview` for live
reloading while writing.

### RevTeX setup

The PDF uses `documentclass: revtex4-2` with the options
`aps, pra, reprint, superscriptaddress`; change `pra` to target another
journal, or `reprint` to `preprint` for a single-column draft. The folder
`_revtex/` holds the glue between Quarto and RevTeX. The file
`before-body.tex` emits `\title`, `\author`, `\affiliation`, `\email` and
the abstract after `\begin{document}`, as RevTeX requires. The file
`preamble.tex` resolves a `longtable*` clash with the `caption` package.
The generated LaTeX is kept in `_manuscript/_tex/` for journal submission.

### Fonts

Text and mathematics are set in STIX Two in both the PDF and the HTML
output. The font files are in `_fonts/`, and they are switched on by
`stix: true` in `_quarto.yml`; set it to `false` to use the default fonts.
The filter `_fonts/stix.lua` loads the fonts in the PDF preamble and, for
HTML, tells MathJax 4 to use its STIX Two math font.

### Plots {#sec-plots}

The first code chunk in this file loads the local package `revtexplot`,
which styles matplotlib figures to match the PDF. It is switched on by
`plot-style: true` in `_quarto.yml`; set it to `false` for matplotlib's
defaults. Figures are one column wide by default and use 8 pt text, the
size of `\footnotesize`, in STIX Two (or Computer Modern with
`stix: false`). They are saved at exactly their set size, so the text in
them matches the captions. The package provides these sizes:

- `rp.COLUMN`: one column, 3.40 × 2.10 in (the default)
- `rp.WIDE`: both columns, 7.06 × 2.35 in
- `rp.figsize(width, aspect)`: `width` is `"column"`, `"wide"` or inches,
  and `aspect` is height / width

For example, `plt.subplots(figsize=rp.figsize("column", 1))` gives a
square one-column figure.

### Writing

Authors, affiliations, e-mail addresses and the abstract are set in the YAML
header. Sections, equations and figures get labels with the prefixes
`sec-`, `eq-` and `fig-`, and are referenced as `@sec-methods`,
`@eq-gaussian` or `@fig-example`. A displayed equation is labelled by
appending `{#eq-name}` after its closing `$$`. Citations use keys from
`references.bib`, e.g. `[@knuth1984]`, and are formatted by BibTeX with
the `apsrev4-2` style. Figures are produced by Python chunks whose
`label` and `fig-cap` options set the reference and caption; see
@sec-results for an example.

### Wide figures and equations

In the two-column `reprint` layout, a figure spans both columns when it
uses RevTeX's `figure*` environment. For a Python chunk, add the options
```python
#| fig-env: "figure*"
#| fig-pos: "t"
```
and create the figure with `plt.subplots(figsize=rp.WIDE)` (see
@sec-plots). For an image file, write
```markdown
![Caption.](figures/wide.pdf){#fig-wide
  fig-env="figure*" fig-pos="t"}
```
Wide figures float to the top of a following page. Always set
`fig-pos: "t"`: Quarto places chunk figures with `[H]` by default, which
makes a `figure*` vanish from the PDF. Do not use `column: page`; it loads
the `sidenotes` package, which stops every `figure*` from spanning both
columns.

A long equation is set across both columns by wrapping it in RevTeX's
`widetext` environment with raw LaTeX blocks:
````markdown
```{=latex}
\begin{widetext}
```
$$
E = \sum_n a_n x^n + \dots
$$ {#eq-wide}
```{=latex}
\end{widetext}
```
````
Labels and cross-references work as usual. The HTML output ignores
`fig-env`, `fig-pos` and the raw LaTeX, so both render normally there.

## Introduction

This is placeholder text for the introduction. Literate programming
[@knuth1984] advocates weaving code and prose into a single document, an idea
that Quarto applies to scientific manuscripts. The typesetting itself is done
by TeX [@knuth1986] and LaTeX [@lamport1994]. Multiple references can be
cited together [@knuth1984; @lamport1994].

## Methods {#sec-methods}

### Inline and displayed mathematics

Inline mathematics is written between single dollar signs, as in
$e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$. Displayed equations are written between double dollar
signs and numbered when given a label, as for the Gaussian integral
$$
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{-a x^2}\, dx = \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{a}},
\qquad a > 0.
$$ {#eq-gaussian}

### Multi-line equations

Long expressions can be split with an `aligned` environment inside a single
labelled equation,
$$
\begin{aligned}
f(x) &= \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{f^{(n)}(x_0)}{n!} (x - x_0)^n \\
     &= f(x_0) + f'(x_0)(x - x_0) + \mathcal{O}\big((x - x_0)^2\big).
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-taylor}

### Cross-references

Equations are referenced as @eq-gaussian and @eq-taylor, sections as
@sec-results, and figures as @fig-example. The numbers are assigned
automatically in every output format.

## Results {#sec-results}

@fig-example is generated by the Python code chunk embedded in the source
file. It shows the damped oscillation
$$
f(t) = e^{-\gamma t} \cos(\omega t).
$$ {#eq-damped}
for three values of the damping rate $\gamma$.

```{python}
#| label: fig-example
#| fig-cap: "Damped oscillations for three values of the damping rate $\\gamma$, with $\\omega = 2\\pi$."
#| echo: false
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

t = np.linspace(0, 4, 400)
omega = 2 * np.pi

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
for gamma in (0.25, 0.5, 1.0):
    ax.plot(t, np.exp(-gamma * t) * np.cos(omega * t), lw=1,
            label=rf"$\gamma = {gamma}$")
ax.set_xlabel("$t$")
ax.set_ylabel("$f(t)$")
ax.legend()
plt.show()
```

@fig-wide spans both columns and shows each damping rate in its own panel.

```{python}
#| label: fig-wide
#| fig-cap: "The oscillations of @fig-example with their envelopes $\\pm e^{-\\gamma t}$ (dashed)."
#| fig-env: "figure*"
#| fig-pos: "t"
#| echo: false
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=rp.WIDE, sharey=True)
for ax, gamma in zip(axes, (0.25, 0.5, 1.0)):
    ax.plot(t, np.exp(-gamma * t) * np.cos(omega * t))
    ax.plot(t, np.exp(-gamma * t), "k--", lw=0.6)
    ax.plot(t, -np.exp(-gamma * t), "k--", lw=0.6)
    ax.set_title(rf"$\gamma = {gamma}$")
    ax.set_xlabel("$t$")
axes[0].set_ylabel("$f(t)$")
plt.show()
```
